subject: Request for penetration test report and remediation update (post-incident)
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@cascadehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Cascade Health Security <security@cascadehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Request for penetration testing report and remediation status (post-incident)

Connor —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Given the anomalous activity we observed on Friday that affects a subset of our integration traffic, my security team is asking for formal documentation from Redwood so we can brief our board and our incident response panel. Specifically, we need: 

- The most recent penetration test report that covers your public-facing inference endpoints (redacted as needed).
- The exact scope of that assessment (external IPs, domains, in-scope services and test dates).
- A remediation status update for any findings classified as Critical or High (including fix dates, mitigation details, and evidence such as patch IDs or ticket links).
- Any retest / verification evidence if available.

I attached a short incident summary from our side (Cascade_Incident_Summary.pdf) to help you triage. Our timeline is tight — we need a redacted report and remediation summary within 48 hours if possible so we can prepare material for an emergency review next week. If there are confidentiality or legal constraints, please let us know the process (DTA/NDA/secure transfer) immediately.

Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Information Security, Cascade Health
jordan.mills@cascadehealth.com
+1 (503) 555-0198

--- Attachment: Cascade_Incident_Summary.pdf (pdf, 127 KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for penetration testing report and remediation status (post-incident)

Jordan —

Thanks for flagging and for the summary — we take this very seriously. I’ve looped in our CS lead (Marissa) and our security/ops lead (Aisha) to coordinate. Initial acknowledgements and next steps: 

1) Acknowledged. We will prioritize providing a sanitized penetration test report and a remediation tracker.
2) We need to sanitize PII and internal identifiers before sharing. Our security team expects to provide a redacted PDF and a remediation tracker with evidence (screenshots of patches / Jira IDs) within 72 hours. If you need faster than that, tell us and we’ll try to compress the timeline.
3) If Cascade requires the full, unredacted report we’ll need an executed DTA or an MoU that specifies allowed recipients and handling. We can provide the redacted version without a DTA.
4) Delivery method: secure SFTP or a locked Drive folder with access logs. Please confirm your preferred transfer method.

I’ll have Marissa and Aisha coordinate the actual artifacts and confirm timelines by EOD.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Request for penetration testing report and remediation status (post-incident)

Connor — quick internal note before we reply to Cascade: 

On Thu, Mar 5, 2026 at 3:10 PM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan —
> 
> Thanks for flagging and for the summary — we take this very seriously. I’ve looped in our CS lead (Marissa) and our security/ops lead (Aisha) to coordinate. Initial acknowledgements and next steps: 
> 
> 1) Acknowledged. We will prioritize providing a sanitized penetration test report and a remediation tracker.

Action items for us (security + product):
- Security to produce a redacted pen test PDF that removes internal IPs, service account names, and customer identifiers. Target: pen-test-report-redacted-v2.pdf.
- Product to export remediation evidence (Jira ticket snapshots, patch IDs, CVE mappings) and assemble remediation-tracker.csv.
- Legal to confirm whether Cascade's request triggers a DTA. If they ask for full report access, we need PO/contracting review.
- Ops to prepare a secure delivery mechanism (SFTP or restricted GDrive with access logs).

Notes on redaction: keep full technical detail for the findings themselves (vectors, exploitability, CVE references) but strip anything that identifies our internal topology or other customers. We can include a short executive summary for board reading.

I’ll assemble the artifacts into the Drive folder (shared link below) and hold until Connor confirms we can send the redacted pack.

Internal link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c (internal security folder)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Security Programs, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@cascadehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Cascade Health Security <security@cascadehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for penetration testing report and remediation status (post-incident)

Connor / Marissa / Aisha —

Thank you for the quick turnaround and for offering a redacted package. Cascade can accept a redacted report plus a remediation tracker for our emergency review. A few clarifications we need included in the package: 

- Explicit scope statement (test dates, in-scope domains/IPs/services).
- For each Critical/High finding: finding ID (or CVE), short technical summary, remediation implemented (with dates), evidence (patch IDs / ticket references).
- Retest evidence or verification steps planned (or a timeline for retest).
- Confirmation whether any customer data was in scope of the original test and whether any data exposure was discovered.

Preferred delivery: secure SFTP (we will provide temp credentials) or the locked Drive link you mentioned with ACLs limited to 5 named recipients. If you can include a checksum and last-modified timestamp for the report file that helps our intake.

Our board briefing is scheduled for Friday afternoon; can you confirm delivery of the redacted report and tracker no later than Thursday EOD (Mar 11)? If Redwood cannot meet that, please say so and provide the earliest possible ETA.

If legal needs a DTA for the unredacted report we can provision one but would prefer to avoid delays if a redacted package suffices.

Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Information Security, Cascade Health
jordan.mills@cascadehealth.com
+1 (503) 555-0198

--- Attachments expected: pen-test-report-redacted-v2.pdf; remediation-tracker.csv
